mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Samoa is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or utility company, to be certified by a Notary Public or competent national authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions alerts, and PEP lists; enhanced due diligence required for each non-resident UBO; any positive match requires immediate disclosure to the Samoa FIU and rejection of the incorporation request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies and Trusts Registry (SICTR) Electronic Name Reservation System – Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Apia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Legal corporate name must be in English or Samoan using Roman script only; Samoan-language names require an accurate certified English translation filed at the same time; diacritical marks should be avoided in the register; the name cannot be identical or nearly identical to an existing registered name or a reserved name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected administratively, the applicant may file a Notice of Appeal with the SICTR within 21 calendar days of the rejection; the appeal must state the legal basis for acceptance under section 11 of the International Companies Act 1987. Alternatively, the agent may submit a new name application. A final administrative appeal may be lodged with the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days if the Registry refuses to reconsider the decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for a Samoa International Company engaged in a high-risk PSP activity; a physical registered office in Samoa operated by a licensed registered agent is mandatory, and the office must have complete, visible business substance including staff and records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximately 75% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months due to the payment gateway/banking AML high-risk classification and expected Central Bank of Samoa licensing review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2013 (Samoa), ss. 6-18 and s. 67 (incorporation, memorandum and articles, registered office and licensed registered agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation as an International Company (Form IC-1), accompanied by the Memorandum and Articles of Association, Statement of Subscribers, Officer Consents, and Registered Agent Consent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the memorandum must state authorized share capital (commonly USD 1,000,000) and at least one share must be issued to a subscriber; no escrow deposit or proof of paid-up capital is required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation application and the Memorandum and Articles of Association filed by the Subscriber be and are hereby ratified and approved in full. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the allotment of one hundred ordinary shares at USD 1.00 each to the Subscriber named in the Statement of Subscribers be and is hereby approved, and the Secretary is directed to issue the corresponding share certificates. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the offices of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [DIRECTOR NAME] be and is hereby appointed the first Director, and [SECRETARY NAME] the first Corporate Secretary, each to hold office in accordance with the Articles of Association, with full authority to open bank accounts and execute all regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Engagement of Licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (SIFA-licensed) and Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed company name is distinguishable on the SIFA register, submit a name reservation application, and appoint a SIFA-licensed registered agent maintaining a physical office in Apia; the agent executes a formal consent to act and confirms service of process arrangements.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Consent of proposed registered agent
Corporate structure and beneficial ownership disclosure
Certified passport copy of the ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an alternate name immediately; if the Registrar issues an objection, submit a fresh preservation request within seven business days or apply for a written waiver where the name qualifies as a minor variation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and SIFA-licensed Registered Agent, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association, Issue the Statement of Subscribers, and obtain execution by the subscriber; if executed outside Samoa, notarize and apostille the signature blocks; the registered agent certifies the documents as compliant with the International Companies Act 2013.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association
Articles of Association
Statement of Subscribers
Consents of proposed directors and corporate secretary
Notarization/apostille of execution pages
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent or notary flags a defect, amend the affected clause, re-execute, and re-notarize the corrected signature page at no additional statutory charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 together with the fully executed Memorandum and Articles, Statement of Subscribers, officer consents, registered agent consent, and payment of the statutory incorporation fee; the Registrar examines compliance and issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation as an International Company)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed)
Statement of Subscribers
Consents of directors and corporate secretary
Consent of licensed registered agent
Certified passport copies of all appointees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any Registrar requisition within fourteen calendar days; provide supplementary evidence of authorization or clarity on clauses; where the application is rejected, correct the omissions and re-file with an expedited review request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation from SIFA, open the statutory minute book and registers, adopt the First Board Resolution in written form, issue share certificates, and file the registered office confirmation with the approved agent.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
First Board Resolution (signed)
Share certificates and register of members
Register of directors and corporate secretary
Notice of registered office and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply to the Registrar for a certificate of correction if any corporate data (name, capital, director particulars) is recorded inaccurately; submit the resolution and registers for administrative endorsement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment Service Provider Licensing and Operational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) and Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Payment Service Provider license application with the CBS under the National Payments System Act 2020 and the Financial Institutions Act 2016; concurrently apply for fire safety clearance and workplace registration; obtain tax-exemption confirmation from the Ministry of Revenue for International Companies.
required_dossiers: Payment Service Provider License application form
Fit and proper declarations for directors and senior officers
AML/CFT compliance manual and risk assessment
Business plan and projected payment volumes
Evidence of card scheme membership (Visa/Mastercard) or sponsorship
Fire Safety Clearance application to SFESA
Ministry of Revenue tax exemption confirmation request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address CBS deficiency letters within thirty calendar days; if licensure is delayed, apply for a temporary incidental authority while supplementing requested governance or anti-money-laundering documentation; appeal adverse determinations to the CBS Board of Review within thirty days of notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Financial Systems and Payments Oversight Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Payment Service Provider Licence under the National Payments System Act 2020 and the Financial Institutions Act 2016 (as applicable)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Registration (low-impact office and IT operation; full EIA Report not required; environmental permit registration applies only if physical server infrastructure or backup generation is installed)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater discharge to municipal sewer per the Water Resources Management Act 2008; standby generator emissions and air quality limits per MNRE ambient air quality guidelines; waste electrical and electronic equipment disposal per Samoa's waste management regulations; no VOC process emissions from payment gateway operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); structural load and electrical installation inspection certificate from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure; occupational health and workplace safety clearance from the Ministry of Health for all operational premises

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of the Independent State of Samoa; online portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company applying for a TIN/VAGST ID must file the prescribed TIN application with the Ministry for Revenue, attaching: (a) certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing under the International Companies Act 1987; (b) details of the registered office and locally appointed registered agent/secretary; (c) certified copies of constitutional documents and the statutory beneficial ownership register; and (d) tax identification data of the foreign parent and merchant counterparties. After verification, the Ministry issues a TIN within approximately five working days. If the International Company makes taxable supplies in Samoa, a separate VAGST registration is required, obligating it to charge, report, and pay VAGST and to retain full records for at least seven years. For wholly offshore payment-acquiring and clearing operations, the International Company should also obtain a written tax-exemption certificate confirming its exempt status; no minimum capital is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - A Samoa International Company is exempt from Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and withholding taxes on offshore income and distributions. Its non-resident owners and cross-border payment-gateway operations are generally outside the territorial tax net, provided no taxable activity is conducted in Samoa. VAGST applies only to taxable supplies connected with Samoa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no US-style check-the-box election and no general hybrid-mismatch election in Samoa. The principal election for the International Company is voluntary VAGST registration where annual taxable turnover does not exceed the WST 100,000 threshold; registration is compulsory above that threshold. The International Company may also elect to document and preserve its exempt status by filing annual statutory returns with the Registrar and, where appropriate, seeking a Ministry for Revenue exemption ruling for the offshore payment-processing services. No group fiscal unity, branch-transfer, or loss-relief election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (approximately USD 35,500) in annual taxable turnover; registration is compulsory once supplies of goods or services in Samoa exceed that threshold, and voluntary registration is permitted below it. A non-resident offshore payment-service provider with no Samoan taxable supplies is not required to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not mandate real-time e-invoicing, digital stamping, or an API-connected fiscal reporting engine at the point of invoicing. Customs export declarations are processed through ASYCUDA World, and VAGST returns are filed electronically through the Ministry for Revenue portal. Taxable suppliers must issue invoices and credit notes containing supplier name, TIN/VAGST ID, date, description of supply, consideration, and VAGST calculated. Electronic records must be retained for tax audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported from Samoa and to services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa where the benefit of the services is not enjoyed in Samoa. Payment-gateway, merchant acquiring, clearing, and settlement services supplied from a Samoa International Company exclusively to non-resident merchants qualify for zero-rating if properly contracted, invoiced to a non-resident, performed offshore, and evidenced by foreign-currency settlement through Visa/Mastercard rails or Fedwire. Financial services that are exempt in the domestic VAGST regime will not produce zero-rated output tax unless the specific service is accepted as an exported taxable service; in either case, the exporter should substantiate the offshore character of the supply to protect input credits and refund positions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World export entry) for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing shipment from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate from a licensed Samoan commercial bank
Signed service agreement and commercial invoice with the non-resident merchant
SWIFT MT103, Fedwire settlement receipt, or Visa/Mastercard settlement statement linking consideration to the invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may scrutinise zero-rated export claims and require the above documents, bank statements, and the registered agent's or payment-service provider's transaction ledger within 180 days of supply. Failure to substantiate export status, or the use of an artificial structure to convert exempt or offshore revenue into a refund, will result in assessment of VAGST at 15% on the full consideration, interest, a tax-shortfall penalty of up to 150%, clawback of refunds, revocation of the International Company's exemption for Samoan-source activity, and possible director liability under the Tax Administration Act 2012 and the International Companies Act 1987. Criminal prosecution is available in cases of fraudulent zero-rating or false documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS; Samoan: Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), Exchange Control Division. Governing instruments: Exchange Control Act 1976; Financial Institutions Act 1996; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (and Regulations 2009); National Payment System Act 2018.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed non-fully convertible currency; the CBS operates an exchange-control regime under which all non-resident payments require CBS approval or delegation to authorized dealers. Current-account items (trade, services, dividends derived from resident sources) are generally approvable; capital-account flows (equity injections, loan repayments, liquidation proceeds) require prior CBS consent. An International Company (IC) carrying on an offshore payment-gateway business exclusively in foreign currency and without Samoa-resident counterparties faces no material convertibility hurdle: it may receive and retain USD in a CBS-approved foreign-currency account and remit profits offshore without enforced conversion to WST; only funds payable to Samoa residents or converted to WST for local expenses trigger the standard surrender and reporting duties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters of goods must collect proceeds within 180 days of shipment and convert 100% to WST through an authorized dealer unless a CBS retention approval is held; service exporters (including payment-processing fee earners) must repatriate proceeds within 180 days of invoice date and likewise surrender or hold under an approved foreign-currency account. The WS_IC is treated as a non-resident IC for exchange-control purposes: its USD fee income may be retained in a designated BSP Samoa foreign-currency account under standing CBS general permission for international companies, subject to quarterly authorized-dealer reporting; conversion of USD to WST for local disbursements is reported by the bank and requires no separate CBS license for amounts below the authorized-dealer threshold.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited — BSP Apia Head Office
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (USD) and Operational Settlement Account (USD/WST multi-currency)
Operational USD Settlement Account (with WST sweep)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Samoa Limited (NBS), Apia

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium onshore; Medium offshore. Samoa has no standalone e-money or EMI licensing regime; CBS regulates remittance and payment businesses indirectly under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and the National Payment System Act 2018. No offshore digital EMI (e.g., Airwallex, Currencycloud-type platforms) may lawfully open a customer-facing Samoa branch or custody client funds without CBS licensing. The legally cleanest structure is: the Samoa IC is licensed or registered as a money-remittance/payment business with CBS and holds its settlement and treasury accounts directly with BSP Samoa, optionally using a licensed NZ/HK/SG EMI purely as disbursement middleware with BSP's informed consent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical interview is effectively mandatory: BSP and SCB require at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-person onboarding meeting in Apia; NBS applies the same standard for high-risk PSP structures. Remote video-KYC is acceptable only for a low-risk IC introduced by a licensed Samoa registered agent under a bank-approved program, and even then notarized passports, a registered-agent certificate, and certified incorporation/good-standing documents must be couriered to the bank. Budget a 3-5 business day Apia visit for the KYC interview and signature verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Samoa IC with zero local staff, non-resident directors, and immediate foreign beneficial owners triggers the 'no physical substance' red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered Agent Certificate under International Companies Act 1987; Certificate of Good Standing; Certificate of Incumbency; certified passports with notarized copies; corporate charter; registered-share register evidencing no bearer shares; group structure chart; two-year audited or management accounts; source-of-wealth statement for each beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 6619 payment-gateway/merchant-acquiring activity classified as High-Risk Special License category under bank AML risk tiers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBS registration or license evidence; AML/CFT compliance manual and sanctions-screening policy; risk-based merchant due-diligence framework; list and risk rating of top merchant counterparties; proof of Visa/Mastercard sponsor-bank or acquiring-bank relationship; conducted media and sanctions checks on merchant principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound liquidity flows from aggregated card settlements or an equity injection originating from a non-bank or crypto-related entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Card-network/acquirer settlement reports for the preceding six months; sponsor-bank statements; invoice-to-settlement reconciliation; source-of-funds declarations for all initial capital contributions; shareholder bank confirmation letters; board resolution authorizing the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholders or offshore trust ownership obscuring control (AML ownership red flag).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial-ownership declarations lodged with the Samoa registered agent and CBS; no-bearer-share certification; organizational chart with control percentages; trust deed summary, trustees, and protector disclosure; signed acknowledgement of CBS beneficial-ownership reporting duties; personal net-worth evidence for all individuals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt IC perceived as a potential tax-evasion conduit or sanctions-circumvention vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax Exemption Certificate or International Company License; business plan proving genuine fee-for-service payment processing for non-resident clients; written confirmation that no business is conducted with Samoa residents; sanctions-screening tool output; auditor's confirmation of non-resident revenue; annual economic-substance filing receipts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 in USD from the corporate shareholder's bank account to Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Ltd, Apia (SWIFT BIC: BOSPSWSM), beneficiary account 'WS_IC Capital Escrow (USD)', remittance field 70 coded 'EQUITY INJECTION / SHARE ALLOTMENT — WS_IC'. The bank files the CBS exchange-control declaration; the IC provides a board resolution, updated registered-share register, registered agent's incumbency certificate, and source-of-funds bank statements. No CBS prior approval is required for receipt while funds remain in USD; any subsequent WST conversion for local professional fees above the USD 50,000 equivalent should be pre-notified to CBS by the authorized dealer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) Cross-border merchant payouts via SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV USD wires through BSP's correspondent banking network (New York and Australia) with payment purpose fields 'PROCESSING FEE' or 'TRADE SETTLEMENT'; (2) Visa/Mastercard scheme settlement files settle via the sponsor/acquirer directly into the WS_IC USD settlement account at BSP, after which WS_IC executes merchant payouts through the same USD clearing line; (3) Commercial letters of credit advised or confirmed by BSP Samoa under UCP600 and URR725, with confirmation by an OECD-based bank where beneficiary risk requires it; (4) Intra-Samoa WST legs clear through CBS-operated national payment-and-settlement infrastructure and are used only for permissible local operating costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward USD/WST up to 12 months with genuine underlying commercial contract (via CBS-authorized dealer BSP or SCB)
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on WST with an offshore OECD bank where onshore deliverable liquidity is unavailable, settled in USD, with CBS notification
Cross-currency swap (USD/NZD/AUD) for intercompany treasury management with prior CBS approval
Vanilla FX option USD/WST on a case-by-case basis through a CBS-approved authorized dealer

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company AnnualGovernment Fee Payment / Licence Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation date; payment due by each anniversary, with a 30-day grace period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee for up to 60 days; thereafter an additional 50% is added. Persistent non-payment triggers administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register and loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies / Samoa Companies Registry, MCIL; coordinated with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit for AML/CFT purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed no later than 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation, together with the annual licence renewal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file an accurate beneficial ownership return is a criminal offence punishable by fines up to WST 10,000 and potential Director disqualification; the company may also be subject to suspension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Compliance Certificate and Statistical Return (for Licensed Payment Service Provider)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Central Bank of Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of each calendar year for the preceding year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts fines under the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act, including penalties up to WST 100,000 for licensed financial service providers; continued non-compliance may result in revocation of the PSP licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Samoa International Company is exempt from the mandatory local statutory audit unless it is licensed or regulated as a bank, insurance undertaking, trust service provider, or financial services entity. A cross-border payment gateway holding a PSP licence is required to undergo an independent annual audit of its financial statements and AML/CFT controls by an approved auditor as a condition of the licence.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) as adopted by Samoa; for small entities, Samoa may permit the IFRS for SMEs framework, but licensed PSPs must use full IFRS for the filing to the Central Bank of Samoa.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Samoa Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017 requires every International Company to keep a beneficial ownership register. Any transfer of shares must be reflected in the register within 21 days, and the annual confirmation return must state the current individuals with significant control as of the anniversary date. Registered agents are obliged to obtain and verify this information annually and to advise the Registrar of any discrepancies.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – 15,000 per year for a licensed PSP entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies (ICs) incorporated under the International Companies Act 2015 are exempt from Samoa income tax on all income derived outside Samoa. A fixed annual government licence fee (ranging from US$200 to US$600 depending on authorised capital) replaces corporate income tax. An IC may also obtain an income tax exemption certificate from the Ministry of Revenue confirming zero effective tax on foreign-source business income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Income Tax Return for Companies (Form IR-2) filed electronically through the Samoa Taxpayer E-Services portal operated by the Ministry of Revenue (MAF). The IC must also file an annual return under the International Companies Act with the Registrar of International Companies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional tax instalments for taxpayers with taxable income exceeding WST 500,000)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final annual income tax return must be filed within six months after the end of the financial year. For an IC with a standard financial year ending 31 December, the due date is 30 June of the following year. Provisional instalments are due on the 20th day of months 4, 7, and 10 during the income year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income derived from Samoa sources (required to be declared even if exempt to establish exempt status)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero or note 'Exempt IC' for income not derived in Samoa; attach schedule of offshore revenues.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt international company income (foreign-source receipts, interest, royalties, fees from cross-border payment services)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the amount in the exemption schedule supported by board minutes and transaction logs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income after applying exemption provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For fully offshore IC, amount should be nil.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions (operating expenses, IT infrastructure, salaries, professional fees) attributable to Samoa-source taxable income only
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must not exceed taxable Samoa-source income; exempt income expenses are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income / loss for the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute after applying carryforward loss rules (5-year limit).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at statutory rate (27%) after tax credits and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For exempt IC, enter zero and attach withholding tax certificates for any Samoa-source royalty/interest if applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 20% of the unpaid tax plus a daily interest charge of 0.5% on the outstanding amount from the due date to the date of payment. Failure to file an IC annual return attracts a penalty of WST 1,000 per month of default plus potential strike-off and director disqualification.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends paid by a Samoa resident company to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's limited network of double taxation agreements (e.g., with Australia and New Zealand) permits reduced dividend withholding tax rates. To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the relevant treaty jurisdiction to the Samoa paying entity before payment. The payer submits a WHT reduction application to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue using Form WHT-3, accompanied by the TRC and a declaration of beneficial ownership. The Ministry issues an approved treaty rate certificate within 15 working days.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest is 15% for payments to non-residents. Under the Samoa-Australia DTA, royalty and interest WHT is reduced to 10%; under the Samoa-New Zealand DTA, interest may be exempt in certain bank financing scenarios and royalties are generally taxed at 5% if beneficial owned by a treaty resident.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Samoa International Company with controlled transactions exceeding WST 15 million per annum (approximately US$5.6 million) is required to prepare a Local File and contribute data to a Master File. An exemption applies for ICs whose gross offshore revenue is below WST 12 million and whose related-party payments are priced using a group policy with full benchmarking.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations (2020) require International Companies deriving income from 'relevant activities' to maintain substantial economic presence in Samoa. Although payment processing is not currently within the enumerated relevant activities, the cross-border payment gateway structure must demonstrate adequate physical presence, active management, and minimum qualified employees in Samoa to avoid being recharacterised as a shell entity. A summary economic substance declaration must be filed annually by the IC's registered agent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating or omitting foreign-source income in the IC exemption return or misrepresenting the payment gateway's central management and control location to avoid the 27% Samoa corporate tax on income actually sourced in Samoa (e.g., acquiring local merchants or processing domestic payments without a resident licence).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to 150% of the evaded tax, daily interest at 2% per month, immediate revocation of the IC tax exemption, and prosecution under Section 111 of the Samoa Income Tax Act 2015. First offence: fine up to WST 1 million; second offence: imprisonment of up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors can be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt if they authorised the evasion. Criminal conviction triggers automatic disqualification from managing any Samoa company, a travel ban pending full restitution, and seizure of personal assets used in the fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company as a pure letterbox for a payment gateway with no real national substance (no officers in Samoa, no board participation, no bookkeeping records held in Samoa, and no demonstrable operational control over merchant acquiring contracts).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations, a financial penalty of up to US$500,000 plus compulsory strike-off from the International Companies Register. Tax authorities may deem the entity tax resident in a foreign jurisdiction, eliminating Samoan treaty access and triggering back-taxes for five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Registered agents and directors face fines of WST 250,000 and up to 5 years' imprisonment for knowingly facilitating a sham. Directors may also be compelled to personally indemnify third-party payment processors for regulatory penalties imposed by Visa, Mastercard, or the Samoa Central Bank.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a cross-border payment gateway without a valid Money Changer / Remittance Licence from the Samoa Financial Services Authority (FSA), or failing to conduct customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, and suspicious activity reporting for high-risk merchant acquiring and cross-border money movement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to US$1 million per breach, immediate suspension of the licence, confiscation of unexplained transaction proceeds, and criminal trial under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2017. The FSA may blacklist the IC, preventing any form of interbank clearing or access to Visa/Mastercard networks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and directors are personally subject to penalties up to WST 300,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years for willful blindness to money laundering. The corporate veil is pierced if anti-money laundering compliance is shown to be a sham; personal bank accounts and foreign passport assets may be frozen under an international mutual legal assistance order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, interest, or royalties to non-resident shareholders without assessing the 15% withholding tax or failing to obtain the applicable double tax treaty reduction certificate from the Samoa Ministry of Revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A 40% administrative penalty on the uncollected withholding tax plus interest at 2% per month from the payment date. The tax remains due even if never collected from the recipient, and the payer loses entitlement to deduct the expense where withholding is absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly cause a corporate distribution without withholding become jointly and severally liable for the full unpaid WHT and penalties. In serious repeat cases, a director may be banned from travelling to Australia and New Zealand through a tax debt recovery mechanism.
